rationale: Oral Sichuan pepper decoction shortened a mouse pole task after pre-exposure dosing. The related Japanese pepper experiment used a distilled intranasal preparation. Neither measured clinical bradykinesia after toasted pepper.

Cold-pressed oil studies use animal recognition tasks. A mixed ketogenic case lists avocado-oil mayonnaise with narrative executive change. Whole fruit and mixed menus have registered outcomes with no available executive estimate for the matched Preiss report. The data cannot assign a direction to the oil claim.

Animal extract work addresses evoked nociception. The two uncontrolled gout decoction reports have follow-up or count and score inconsistencies and unresolved independence. Both use boiled leaves and neither has a Parkinson comparison.

Flaxseed table oil has a small healthy-adult fluency difference and an inconclusive total frontal battery. A pooled omega-3 cohort has faster global cognitive decline without a separate oil estimate. A new executive-composite registry has no results. These measures and exposures leave the frozen comparison unresolved.

A Parkinson bundled menu lists spinach with no preparation or facial-expression item result. Aged-rat conditioned eyeblink learning and a separate conference abstract about preferred omelets do not measure Parkinson facial expressiveness.

Two Parkinson mixed menus mention cucumber without a separate posture effect. Exact source bodies yield sea cucumber and unrelated gait or diagnostic matches. The lead-exposure rat extract paper gives no accessible assay name or arm estimates and cannot resolve effects of raw cucumber.

Several extracts improve movement proxies in toxin-exposed animals. Open-field exploration distance differs from walking velocity. No clinical walking-speed effect is isolated after dried culinary cilantro.

The Perilla eye trial uses aqueous extract with contradictory reported sample size and an ocular endpoint. Seed-peptide studies and athlete leaf-flavonoid results measure exercise performance. In the gastrectomy trial the registry and protocol disagree on perilla and have no fatigue results.
